column3: NASB places “saying,” which opens v. 2 in the Greek, at the end of this verse.
NASB renders “the kingdom of the heavens” as “the kingdom of heaven” and “has drawn near” as “is at hand.”
“Has been spoken of” becomes “referred to … when he said”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“fruit,” singular); “fruit in keeping with” renders “fruit worthy of.”
NASB renders “to carry” the sandals as “to remove.”
NASB has “the barn” without “his,” like the critical text.
Close to the Greek; the aorist “I was well pleased” is rendered “I am well-pleased.”
